title: By the Stone Fountain  (Junto a la fuente de piedra)

segments.t: El agua clara murmura suavemente en el pilón de piedra tallada de la calle Linden. Hannah y Caleb comparan la tarjeta en acuarela con el borde de piedra mientras Arthur mira con entusiasmo un estrecho callejón lateral. Escucha primero toda la escena.
Look at the left side of the watercolor sketch — there is a tiny carved leaf!
Walk around the dry side of the basin, Hannah; do you see it on the stone?
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
Are you sure about this narrow lane, Arthur? My compass says that bends south.
I have lived on Linden Street for twenty years, Caleb, and alleys beat compasses!
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Arthur?
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighborhood lane?
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence — where are we going?!
Analicemos ahora la conversación junto a la fuente de piedra paso a paso.
Look at the left side of the watercolor sketch — there is a tiny carved leaf!
'¡Miren el lado izquierdo del boceto en acuarela: hay una diminuta hoja tallada!'
Walk around the dry side of the basin, Hannah; do you see it on the stone?
'Rodea el lado seco del pilón, Hannah; ¿la ves en la piedra?'
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
'¡Justo aquí debajo del caño! ¡Una hoja de piedra que apunta hacia el noroeste subiendo la suave colina!'
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
'Déjenme leer la segunda tarjeta: «Sigan la hoja hasta que doce campanadas proyecten una sombra recta».'
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
'¡Doce campanadas! ¡Tiene que ser la antigua torre del reloj municipal, tres manzanas más arriba!'
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
'¿Tres manzanas subiendo por la calle principal? ¡Qué disparate, conozco un atajo de dos minutos!'
Are you sure about this narrow lane, Arthur? My compass says that bends south.
'¿Está seguro de esta callejuela estrecha, Arthur? Mi brújula indica que se desvía hacia el sur.'
I have lived on Linden Street for twenty years, Caleb, and alleys beat compasses!
'¡Llevo veinte años viviendo en la calle Linden, Caleb, y los callejones les ganan a las brújulas!'
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Arthur?
'¿Se acordó de bajarse las gafas de lectura antes de elegir ese giro, Arthur?'
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighborhood lane?
'¿Quién necesita gafas de lectura para reconocer una callejuela del barrio perfectamente recta?'
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
'Muy bien, encabece la expedición, capitán, mientras yo anoto cada giro en mi cuaderno.'
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence — where are we going?!
'¡A la izquierda pasando las macetas, otra vez a la izquierda pasando la valla verde: ¿adónde vamos?!'
Escuchemos toda la escena una vez más.
Look at the left side of the watercolor sketch — there is a tiny carved leaf!
Walk around the dry side of the basin, Hannah; do you see it on the stone?
Right here under the spout! A stone leaf pointing northwest up the gentle hill!
Let me read Card Two: Follow the leaf until twelve chimes cast a straight shadow.
Twelve chimes! That has to be the old municipal clock tower three blocks up!
Three blocks up the main street? Nonsense, I know a two-minute shortcut!
Are you sure about this narrow lane, Arthur? My compass says that bends south.
I have lived on Linden Street for twenty years, Caleb, and alleys beat compasses!
Did you remember to pull your reading glasses down before choosing that turn, Arthur?
Who needs reading glasses to recognize a perfectly straight neighborhood lane?
All right, lead the expedition, Captain, while I count every turn in my notebook.
Left past the flower pots, left again past the green fence — where are we going?!
Ignorando tanto la brújula de latón como sus propias gafas de lectura, Arthur guía con orgullo al grupo por un callejón serpenteante. Nos vemos en la próxima escena.
See you next time!
